\section[(controlled location question)]{Your first Tamil question from meaning}

\label{lesson:TA-W281-enge-controlled-question}



\begin{quote}
Close the earlier lessons. Recall \textbf{tea} and the place question \textbf{where?} without writing either one yet.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — assemble one familiar question}
From meaning alone, write \textbf{Where is the tea?} There is no word bank, romanization, or copyable sentence. Choose the two familiar pieces, put them in Tamil order, and add the question mark. This first composition is untimed: finish the attempt before checking the earlier lessons.

\subsection*{Your turn — repair one difference}
Check the thing, place question, word boundary, and punctuation separately. Repair the first difference and write the whole question once more from meaning.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What made this composition rather than copying? (\textbf{You selected and ordered two known pieces from meaning, with no visible Tamil answer.})

One controlled line closes this writing rung. It does not prove A1 attainment, readiness, human validation, or completion of the later timed writing task.
\end{tcolorbox}
